Reading: all six criteria PASS. Opposite 6D chirality for the singlets gives three left-handed doublets and three right-handed singlets per field, the SM hypercharges, and an allowed scalar Yukawa with a constant, tachyon-free Higgs. The Yukawa matrices are diagonal with three equal entries, so there's no generation splitting on the round sphere. The irreducible 6D anomalies cancel only with nu included. U(1)_X still needs Green-Schwarz. This is a toy and derives nothing.

Degenerate generations [standard] (Helios, note 1): the three generations are the j = 1 triplet of the sphere's SO(3), acting as a rotation combined with a gauge transformation because of the flux. That makes SO(3) an exact flavour symmetry, which forces the three equal singular values. The metric side also gives flavour-changing KK vectors at about 1/R. Splitting the generations needs SO(3) breaking (a squashed sphere, a rugby ball with conical tips, or a localised source); that is a separate later step and is not computed here.

Units [standard] (Helios, note 2): in 6D, [y_6] = -1 (a length), because [psibar psi H] = 5 + 2 = 7 against an action density of dimension 6. With unit-normalised harmonics on a radius-R sphere, y_4 = y_6 * (1/(2 sqrt(pi))) * (1/R). The overlap fixes the coupling ratios, not their overall size. The up, down and lepton 6D couplings are free [assumed input].
